speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. To better understand the timeline and severity of your symptoms, have you noticed any specific rash patterns or lesions developing since the fever started? Also, have you experienced joint pain or a stiff neck?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scarlet Fever (Group A Streptococcal Pharyngitis). Given the classic presentation of fever, headache, rhinorrhea, followed by a diffuse pruritic rash and the specific description of a facial rash sparing the perioral area, this is highly suggestive of scarlet fever. I would like to confirm this with a throat culture and rapid strep test, and request images of the rash to look for the characteristic "sandpaper" texture or Pastia's lines. REQUEST TEST: Throat_Culture_and_Rapid_Strep_Test; REQUEST IMAGES: Rash_Close_Up.
